line.what: Of MASCALI, both living and working there in October 1872 — he a bracciante, she a contadina. Named without «fu» in an act that writes «fu» for a witness two lines above, so the absence is a statement. Neither has been found in any register of any of the four towns.

Of PIEDIMONTE ETNEO, and BOTH DEAD by October 1872 — «figlia del fu GAETANO, e di fu MARIA CURRENTI». Gaetano is also the father named in his daughter's birth entry of 1848, which is what ties the birth to the marriage.
line.src: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20; Nati 1848 atto 45

line.what: Married at Piedimonte Etneo on 7 OCTOBER 1872 at nine in the morning. He thirty-one, a bracciante, «domiciliato e residente a MASCALI» and «nato a GIARRE»; she twenty-four, born at Piedimonte in 1848. The family's export calls them «John Nicotra» and «Venera Cassaneti» and gives neither a date.
line.src: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 and Matrimoni allegati fascicolo 20

line.what: Born at MASCALI on 8 DECEMBER 1875 at half past nine in the evening, in contrada Sopra Pietrafitta, and registered two days later by her father in person. Married Salvatore Mazza about 1900; widowed 1929; sailed to Sydney on 20 April 1962 at about eighty-six, to her sons; died at Brisbane in 1963 and lies at Nudgee.

Nicotra Carmela, atto 228, 1 May 1820. THE NAME IS RIGHT AND THE GENERATION IS NOT: Giovanni's father Rosario was a bracciante still working in 1872, and a man fathering a child in 1820 would be past seventy-five by then. A grandfather-generation namesake is exactly what Sicilian naming custom predicts, and custom is not a document
